edges.effect_quant: The strongest quantitative studies point in a protective direction, but the pooled magnitude varies across populations and methods.
edges.mechanism: Self-sampling expands access to HPV testing, which matters because persistent high-risk HPV detection is the gatekeeper for preventing invasive cervical cancer.
edges.summary: The anchor for this edge is the 2026 Hallsson systematic review in BMC Health Serv Res, which suggests that hpv self- sampling tracks with lower risk or better outcomes for cervical cancer. Later papers point in much the same direction, so the live uncertainty is usually about effect size or which subgroups carry the signal most strongly.
edges.caveats: Healthier-user bias, screening intensity, and baseline risk can all inflate apparent benefit in observational work, so the magnitude should be read conservatively.
